description_short.value: Koforidua-based maker of intravenous fluids and small-volume injectables, traded on the Ghana Alternative Market; loss-making in 2024-2025 and recapitalising in 2026.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Intravenous Infusions PLC 2025 Annual Report (GSE PR 147/2026: directors' report, principal activities and going concern) and GSE PR 088/2026 and PR 455/2026

description_full.value: Intravenous Infusions PLC manufactures intravenous infusion fluids and small-volume injectables at its factory in Koforidua, in Ghana's Eastern Region, and sells them in Ghana and elsewhere in West Africa; the company dates its business to 1969. Its production is certified by the Food and Drugs Authority, and it owns a small retail and wholesale subsidiary, FlexPharm Ltd. The shares have traded on the Ghana Alternative Market since December 2015. At the end of 2025 the largest holders were AI Acquisitions Company Limited (22.9%) and National Investment Bank (13.0%), with members of the Appenteng family among the other large holders. After a profit of GHS 2.5 million in 2023, revenue fell from GHS 31.4 million to GHS 9.3 million in 2025 as working-capital shortages held back imports of raw materials. The company lost GHS 0.6 million in 2024 and GHS 4.6 million in 2025, and its 2025 accounts drew attention to doubt over its ability to continue as a going concern. In February 2026 shareholders approved a GHS 50 million rights issue and private placement. They also approved converting GHS 5.0 million of loans from CCM Healthcare Investments and AI Acquisitions into shares; the conversion took effect on 9 August 2026 and raised stated capital to GHS 16.4 million. The company reported a small profit for the first half of 2026, on lower revenue of GHS 4.3 million. Leon Kendon Appenteng became chairman in September 2026, and Ernst & Young was appointed auditor at the October 2026 AGM.
